fields.v: Agentic Agile-V (Agile-V lifecycle backbone + SCOPE-V micro-cycle: Specify, Constrain, Orchestrate, Prove, Evolve, Verify); builds on the author's Agile-V [1]. No version

Reviewed task/execution brief (objective, scope, non-goals, affected modules, dependencies, acceptance criteria, required evidence); minimum input artefact package (Table I: intent and scope, acceptance criteria, architecture context, constraints, execution context, evidence requirement, risk class); feature, bug and hardware/firmware brief templates; minimal repository instructions (e.g., AGENTS.md); evidence bundle for R2/R3 (brief + requirement IDs, plan, commands and test results, diff summary, trace acceptance criteria -> tests, reviewer decision, rollback path)

Macro: Agile-V increments traceable to requirements, design, implementation, verification, approval, audit. Micro (SCOPE-V): Specify -> Constrain -> Orchestrate (inspect, summarise, plan, small slices, local checks, diff summary) -> Prove (tests, static analysis, simulation, HIL per risk) -> Evolve (feed learning back to instructions/templates/tests) -> Verify (recurring). Conversation-to-contract gate between exploratory dialogue and implementation. Task workflows for features (9 steps), bug fixes (8 steps), testing, hardware

Conversation-to-contract gate (brief reviewed before implementation); risk-adaptive human gates (Table II): R0 optional review, R1 normal code review, R2 mandatory reviewer approval, R3 explicit sign-off and release gate; human review for architecture/security in feature workflow; human approval for state-changing actions; human approval and baseline update in Fig. 1

Not stated in Böckeler terms. 'Do not let an agent implement from a long chat. Let it implement from a reviewed brief'; briefs per task with traceability and Evolve step updating baselines (closest to spec-first, draft)

rev.why: Classification is the reader's: briefs are reviewed before implementation and not kept as source (spec-first), but the Evolve step feeds learning back into repository instructions/templates and Agile-V keeps increments traceable to requirements, which could be read as spec-anchored

Not stated by the author. Reviewed briefs drive each task and are not kept as source (spec-first), but the Evolve step feeds learning back into repository instructions/templates and Agile-V keeps increments traceable to requirements (p. 3-4), which a reader could call spec-anchored

Not stated by the author. Each task is implemented from a reviewed brief (spec-first), but the Evolve step feeds learning back into repository instructions, templates, tests and baselines and Agile-V keeps increments traceable to requirements (p. 3-4), which a reader could call spec-anchored

Synthesis and process proposal, not a benchmark; fast-moving field, point estimates may change; productivity studies and hardware benchmarks heterogeneous; framework must be validated empirically across teams, repositories, tools and hardware domains. Research agenda: do structured briefs beat conversational prompts; minimum useful repository instructions; independent agentic test generation and defect escape; which task classes benefit or are slowed by overhead; evidence bundles vs verification debt; hardware evidence quality
